titulo.texto: Maximilian and Carlota in the Garden

frase_gancho.texto: In eighteen sixty-five, the emperors of Mexico chose this garden to spend the summer and hold concerts by the pond.

puente_narrativo.texto: If you want an extra, the last stop is optional: Cantinflas’s rest house, on Benito Juárez Boulevard. It is not always open.

guion_corto.texto: In eighteen sixty-five, a European emperor chose this garden as a summer home. Maximilian of Habsburg and his wife, Carlota, chose it after returning from a trip to Yucatán. With them, the old Borda house became the Imperial Palace, and stopped functioning as a hotel. They held large gatherings and concerts by the pond. It was a brief episode: Maximilian ruled Mexico for little more than three years. The garden later received other visitors, such as Francisco I. Madero, Emiliano Zapata and Porfirio Díaz. Today it is a cultural center with exhibitions, a bookstore and an open-air auditorium. It is a good place to think about how power and nature meet in a single landscape.

guion_largo.texto:
Maximilian of Habsburg was an Austrian archduke who came to Mexico in eighteen sixty-four to be emperor. His wife, Carlota, was the daughter of the king of Belgium. The two looked for a place to rest outside the capital, and found it in Cuernavaca.

In eighteen sixty-five they chose this garden as a summer home, after their trip to Yucatán. The old Borda house, which until then had operated as a hotel, became the Imperial Palace. Another source indicates that between eighteen sixty-four and eighteen sixty-six the emperor used the Palace of Cortés as a summer residence. The sources do not agree on that detail, so this stop focuses on the garden.

Life in the garden with the emperors was one of parties. Large gatherings and concerts were held over the pond. Imagine the lake with lights and musicians, and the court strolling along the terraces. It is a very European image for a Mexican garden, and that is part of its interest.

To understand why they chose this place, think about what Cuernavaca offered: mild climate, water, shade and flowers. They were reasons of rest, but also of taste. A European court looked for a landscape where it could feel at home.

As you walk, try to locate the main house and the lake. Imagine the walks and the evenings between one and the other. That is how you understand why a garden could also serve as a political stage.

There is a detail worth keeping in mind. Maximilian and Carlota arrived in a country in the middle of a dispute. Their stay in Cuernavaca was a rest within a political project that did not last. It is a pleasure garden that was born from mining wealth and served a passing court.

The episode was short. Carlota traveled to Europe in eighteen sixty-six to ask for help and never returned to Mexico. Maximilian was shot in Querétaro in eighteen sixty-seven. With his death the empire ended.

The garden went on being an important place. According to one source, it later received Porfirio Díaz, Francisco I. Madero and Emiliano Zapata. It is a list that crosses very different projects for the country: the empire, the Porfiriato, the Revolution. One and the same garden saw them all.

Today it is called the Jardín Borda Cultural Center. It has exhibition rooms, a bookstore and an open-air auditorium, where painting, sculpture, photography, dance, theater and concerts are presented. It is classified as a historic monument.

The question this stop leaves is simple. Why do the powerful always choose the same places? A mild climate, water, shade and flowers explain a good deal. But as you walk here, you can also think about who made that beauty possible. The gardeners, the bricklayers and the mine workers who paid for everything do not appear in the chronicles, but they were there.

texto: Find the pond and try to imagine an imperial court concert over the water
Think about the three eras this garden saw: viceregal, imperial and revolutionary
Look at the terraces and work out from which one the party would be best seen

texto.pregunta: Myth: Maximilian lived in Cuernavaca until his death.
texto.respuesta: Reality: He used the garden as a summer home. He was shot in Querétaro in eighteen sixty-seven.
